passages.note: Bill overview names him a co-sponsor of the ESA expansion, signed into law as Chapter 388.
House Third Reading roll call records his Y on final passage; 26 of 60 voted No, so this is not near-unanimous.
passages.actor_quote: KAISER Y KAVANAGH Y LIGUORI N

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve.
passages.note: Enacted text of the single-subject ESA bill: every student eligible to enroll in a public school becomes a qualified student, and account monies pay "Tuition or fees at a qualified school", defined as "a nongovernmental primary or secondary school" barred only from race, color or national origin discrimination, so religious schools are not excluded.

rows.reasoning: Kavanagh co-sponsored HB 2853 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading (31-26), a single-subject bill whose new section 15-2401.01 makes any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" a qualified student, with account monies paying "Tuition or fees at a qualified school", defined as "a nongovernmental primary or secondary school" that is not barred from being religious. That is universal eligibility with the money following the student, matching "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family". Acts from his Arizona House term count for this Senate seat under the same-legislature rule.
